componentPlan.focusQuote: Once your teen has a steady job, help them set up a savings program so that at least 10 percent of earnings goes directly into their savings account.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Checks core savings facts about percent saved and emergency targets before deeper comparison

componentPlan.focusQuote: If they set aside $100 every year starting at age 14, they'd have about $23,000 at age 65.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Contrasts early and late starting ages on shared yearly saving and growth over time

overview.headline: Teen saving habits for emergencies and early compound growth

keyPoints.point: Set up a savings program that puts at least 10 percent of earnings directly into savings
keyPoints.quote: help them set up a savings program so that at least 10 percent of earnings goes directly into their savings account.

keyPoints.point: Aim to keep at least three months worth of living expenses saved for an emergency
keyPoints.quote: have at least three months’ worth of living expenses saved up in case of an emergency.

keyPoints.point: Compound interest means earning interest on both saved money and prior interest earned
keyPoints.quote: Compound interest is when your child earns interest on both the money they save and the interest they earn.

keyPoints.point: Starting early lets money set aside every year grow to about a larger amount over time
keyPoints.quote: If they set aside $100 every year starting at age 14, they'd have about $23,000 at age 65.

keyTerms.gloss: A plan that moves earnings directly into savings for emergencies
keyTerms.quote: help them set up a savings program so that at least 10 percent of earnings goes directly into their savings account.

keyTerms.gloss: Household living costs used to size emergency savings
keyTerms.quote: have at least three months’ worth of living expenses saved up in case of an emergency.

keyTerms.gloss: Interest earned on saved money plus prior interest
keyTerms.quote: Compound interest is when your child earns interest on both the money they save and the interest they earn.

keyTerms.gloss: A retirement account at work with possible employer matching
keyTerms.quote: they may be offered a retirement account at work called a 401(k).

keyTerms.gloss: Employer incentive to encourage saving enough for maximum matching
keyTerms.quote: so it’s smart to save at least enough for the maximum matching contribution.

analysis.pageCoverage: Explains teen emergency savings targets and safe accounts plus retirement matching and early compound growth with examples.
